docs.summary: Humanoid foot placement: moves each foot by the height of the ground under it rather than pinning it there, so a lifted foot stays lifted. The hips drop so the leg over lower ground can reach, planted feet tilt onto the slope, and every offset is smoothed over time so steps do not pop.
Whether the hips move down, or up, to keep both feet reachable.
Seconds for a foot to cover half the distance to a new ground height. Zero snaps.
Seconds for the hips to cover half the distance to a new height. Zero snaps.
The steepest a planted foot tilts to follow the ground, in degrees.
How high a foot lifts, in character units, before it stops tilting onto the ground.
Forgets the smoothed offsets, so the next solve starts on the ground it finds.
